summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' in Feb 2026 as the paradigm of humans directing AI agents for extended periods. AutoResearch is an associated open-source harness for autonomous overnight experiments.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — philosophical framing and experiment harness; AgentForge already implements agentic orchestration for code issues

summary: Proposes a dual-memory design pairing character-and-scene episodic memory with a graph-based semantic memory store for agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — episodic memory design maps to run-outcome episodic memory work, but that is already tracked by HID-188

source: AdaMem: multi-tier agent memory (Tsinghua + Tencent, March 2026)
summary: Organizes agent memory into working, episodic, persona, and graph-based tiers. Published March 2026 from Tsinghua and Tencent, targeting dialogue history management.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — reinforces the episodic+semantic split; HID-188 tracks run-outcome episodic memory; executor skill injection is a known small gap

source: Prime Agent by Prime Intellect (open-source, Aug 2026)
summary: MIT-licensed self-improving coding and research harness with a persistent IPython kernel where tools, skills, and sub-agents operate as Python code. Self-refining loop revises outputs within a session.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — interesting self-improvement loop, but AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses (not Python kernel); adapting would require significant architecture change. Backlog also full (11 open issues).

source: Evolve Loop: community Claude Code / Codex plugin (June 2026)
summary: 4-agent, 5-phase plugin for Claude Code/Gemini CLI/Codex CLI that autonomously discovers, builds, audits, and ships codebase improvements using Reflexion and double-loop learning.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — targets the CLI tools AgentForge uses as subprocesses; pattern is interesting but operates at a different abstraction layer. Out of scope for AgentForge's orchestration layer.

source: INTENT: Budget-aware agent planning with Monte Carlo lookahead (arXiv 2602.11541)
summary: Inference-time planner using a learned world model and Monte Carlo lookahead to estimate tool costs and enforce hard token/cost budget constraints. Reports strict feasibility on cost-augmented StableToolBench.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — token/cost budget enforcement is a gap, but HID-163 (per-run token cost and latency telemetry) is the prerequisite and is explicitly deferred until telemetry data exists. Proposing budget enforcement before telemetry ships is against project rules.

source: BAGEN: Budget interval estimation during agent execution (arXiv 2606.00198, May 2026)
summary: Finds frontier LLMs are consistently over-optimistic about remaining budget and continue spending on tasks unlikely to succeed. Proposes mid-execution budget interval estimation to cut wasted tokens.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — empirical evidence that agents overspend reinforces value of HID-163 (token telemetry). Budget estimation specifically deferred until telemetry exists per project rules.

source: LangGraph 2026 patterns: graph-based flow, MCP/A2A protocols
summary: 2026 LangGraph usage patterns: graph-based branching/looping/checkpoints, four multi-agent archetypes (subagents, handoffs, routers, custom workflows), and MCP/A2A protocol integration.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge has its own deterministic state machine; LangGraph is a competing framework. Patterns are well-known and don't add to AgentForge's verified gaps.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA (April 2026, successor to AutoGen)
summary: Microsoft placed AutoGen in maintenance mode (Oct 2025) and shipped Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA on April 2, 2026 as the enterprise successor. AutoGen still receives bug/security fixes.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocess model (Claude Code, Codex), not this framework. No actionable adoption path.

summary: CrewAI continues active development (reported v1.15.18, Aug 2026) and is the most actively maintained Python multi-agent framework. Recommended for new Python multi-agent projects.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses TypeScript/CLI subprocess model; CrewAI is a Python multi-agent framework. No direct adoption path.
